newsitem.title: UK: Colombia FinMin hopes for lower central bank rates.
newsitem.headline: Colombia FinMin hopes for lower central bank rates.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said in an interview on Friday he was hopeful central bank rates would fall by two to three percentage points in February.

"The main constraint (to further interest rate falls) is central bank rates," he told Reuters. "If these continue to fall there will be no problem. We hope they will fall by two to three percentage points, hopefully this month."
Colombia introduced an emergency package of reforms in January to curb the government's fiscal deficit and stem the heavy flow of dollars into the country.
The peso has fallen sharply since then, and Ocampo said interest rates had also gone down.

"Interest rates have continued to fall but now they are constrained by central bank rates. The central bank keeps the one-day deposit rate at 23 percent and the 90-day deposit rate at 25 percent, and other rates are very close to this," he said.
Ocampo was in London for investor presentations ahead of a $750 million 10-year global bond due for launch next week.
